# SQueryContainer `<s-query-container>`

Turns an element into a size container so its children can adapt to its width with container queries. `SQueryContainer` is the typed Vue 3 wrapper for Shopify's Polaris `<s-query-container>` web component.

```ts
import { SQueryContainer } from 'polaris-vue-elements'
```

## Best practices

- **Adapt to the container, not the viewport.** A query container lets components respond to the width of their container. That helps components that show up in places of different widths, like a product card in a sidebar or in the main column.
- **Name containers when there's more than one.** If several query containers need different queries, give each a descriptive `containerName` so you can target it; unnamed containers all answer the same queries.
- **Put responsive values on props.** The container provides the context Polaris components use to resolve responsive prop values, such as `padding="@container (inline-size > 500px) large-500, none"`, so you don't write container query CSS yourself.
- **Use them only where needed.** Every query container makes the browser track its size and apply conditional styles, so add one where you need container-based responsiveness rather than wrapping every element.

```vue
<SQueryContainer>
  <SBox padding="@container (inline-size > 500px) large-500, none">
    <!-- … -->
  </SBox>
</SQueryContainer>
```

See [Shopify's best practices for `<s-query-container>`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/latest/web-components/layout-and-structure/query-container#best-practices) for the full guidance.

## Example

<script setup>
import SQueryContainerDemo from '../examples/demos/SQueryContainerDemo.vue'
</script>

<!-- Drag the bottom-right handle of the dashed box to resize it and watch the text
     inside switch based on container inline-size, not viewport width. -->
<div class="demo-surface">

<SQueryContainerDemo />

</div>

```vue
<script setup>
import { SQueryContainer, SText } from 'polaris-vue-elements'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="query-resize-wrapper">
    <SQueryContainer containerName="docs-demo">
      <SText class="wide-only">Wide layout (container inline-size ≥ 320px)</SText>
      <SText class="narrow-only">Narrow layout (container inline-size &lt; 320px)</SText>
    </SQueryContainer>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.query-resize-wrapper {
  resize: horizontal;
  overflow: auto;
  inline-size: 400px;
  max-inline-size: 100%;
  min-inline-size: 160px;
  border: 1px dashed #8c9196;
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 12px;
}
.narrow-only {
  display: none;
}
/* Queries the container established by SQueryContainer via its containerName prop. */
@container docs-demo (inline-size < 320px) {
  .wide-only {
    display: none;
  }
  .narrow-only {
    display: block;
  }
}
</style>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `containerName` | `string` | An identifier for this container that you can reference in CSS container queries to apply styles based on this specific container's size. All query container components automatically receive a container name of `s-default`. You can omit the container name in your queries, so `@container (inline-size <= 300px)` is equivalent to `@container s-default (inline-size <= 300px)`. When you provide a custom `containerName`, it's added alongside `s-default`. For example, `containerName="product-card"` results in `s-default product-card` being set on the `container-name` CSS property, allowing you to target this container with `@container product-card (inline-size <= 300px)`. Learn more about the [container-name property](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/container-name). |
| `id` | `string` | A unique identifier for the element. |

## Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | The content displayed within the query container component, which enables container queries for responsive styling based on the container's size rather than the viewport. |
